title: whois
description: Identity lookup behavior across DNS configurations

tests.name: domain not configured for triauth returns status -1
configured domain, unknown identifier returns status 0
per-test dnsEntries patch can NXDOMAIN a previously known domain

triauth record whose value carries a port (auth.porthost.example:8443) does not qualify as an endpoint host — Helpers.isDomainName rejects it in AuthenticationEndpoint.resolve(), domain reports status -1

triauth record without a mode option runs the domain in private mode by default - whois without a lookup code reports status 0 and no identity domain, and the endpoint options report the defaults (mode=private, include=any)
triauth record with mode=Public (uppercase) configures the endpoint but derives no identity domain - mode values are literal and case-sensitive; whois reports status 0 with the value verbatim
triauth record with an unregistered mode (mode=unknownmode) configures the endpoint but derives no identity domain - whois reports status 0 with the value verbatim

triauth record whose value carries a path (auth.pathhost.example/auth) does not qualify as an endpoint host — Helpers.isDomainName rejects it in AuthenticationEndpoint.resolve(), domain reports status -1

triauth record whose value is an exotic IPv4 notation (0x7f.0x1) does not qualify as an endpoint host — the numeric-final-label guard in Helpers.isDomainName rejects it in AuthenticationEndpoint.resolve(), domain reports status -1

triauth record whose value carries a punycode label (xn--mller-kva.de) does not qualify as an endpoint host — Helpers.isDomainName blocks xn-- labels in AuthenticationEndpoint.resolve(), domain reports status -1

triauth record with an uppercase endpoint host (AUTH.Uppercase.Example) is accepted case-insensitively and the endpoint URL is lowercased — src/authentication_endpoint.js compares candidate.hostname to value.toLowerCase()
unknown option on the triauth record (color=blue) is retained in authenticationEndpoint.options and selects nothing — unknown endpoint options are non-critical in protocol v1
known identifier returns status 1 with public profile and devices
SECURITY: endpoint triauth record with dnssec:false caps the resolution-level secure to false even though the key records are DNSSEC-validated
SECURITY: uv=required on a non-webauthn (es256) key is unenforceable and taints the keyGroup -> device excluded from devices - fail closed
key record with type=ed25519 forms a valid device listing (requires the ed25519 verifier to be registered)
SECURITY: uv=required on an ed25519 (non-webauthn) key is unenforceable and taints the keyGroup -> device excluded from devices - fail closed

SECURITY: split key group with only its final fragment published (laptop[2/2] alone, no laptop[1/2]) is not a device — validity requires every declared slot populated (populated-slot count at src/identity_keys.js:153-157, not keys.length, which the lone last-index write already inflates to keyCount), so the incomplete group is excluded from devices - fail closed
publicProfile recognizes name/initials and passes through x- extensions; unrecognized keywords (incl. former 'roles'/'title') and over-long x- keys are dropped
publicProfile value keeps '=' text outside the trailing option run intact (mid-record tokens are not options)
trailing-run parsing: sub-token '=' (a+b=c) stays value text; a trailing x- option on a key record is retained verbatim (no decoding at the record layer) and leaves the deviceTag unchanged
option values are literal - x-note=bad%0Aline is retained verbatim (%0A is two characters, not a newline; nothing percent-decodes at the record layer), and the record stays effective
a profile value with a malformed percent escape (name 50% off) fails its decoding and the record contributes nothing; sibling records unaffected
SECURITY: a publicProfile keyword appearing more than once is dropped entirely (ambiguous; no first/last-wins) for both reserved and x- keywords
SECURITY: a publicProfile value longer than the byte cap is rejected (not truncated)
SECURITY: the number of distinct x- extensions is capped (only the first publicProfileMaxExtensions are kept)

record keys are matched case-sensitively: an uppercase 'NAME' record is not a recognized profile key (ignored for the profile) but is still a well-formed record, so the identity EXISTS with an empty profile (identity existence needs only one well-formed record, whatever its key)
an uppercase 'TRIAUTH' record key does not qualify as an Endpoint Record (case-sensitive record-key match) - the domain is not configured, status -1
a record consisting only of options (name x-a=1 leaves an empty value after the trailing option run) is ignored as a whole; the sibling initials record is unaffected
an option key longer than 255 bytes makes the whole record ignored (the option-key Normal-String cap); the sibling initials record is unaffected
profile values percent-decode where they are consumed: 'name John%20Doe' publishes the display string 'John Doe'
a literal percent in a profile value is published as %25 ('x-slogan 50%25 off' -> '50% off'); machine values never decode, so they need no such escape
a profile value with non-ASCII Unicode letters (name Zoë Müller) is a Normal String and is delivered verbatim
an x- profile record key longer than 64 bytes is not accepted as an extension field (record ignored); the sibling initials record is unaffected
a profile value of exactly 255 bytes (the cap) is kept - strict-greater check, boundary companion of the over-cap rejection case
an endpoint host label of 64 characters exceeds the 63-character DNS label cap - the record does not qualify, status -1
an endpoint host whose final label is a single character (auth.x) violates the 2-character final-label minimum - the record does not qualify, status -1
an endpoint host label of exactly 63 characters (the DNS label cap) qualifies - boundary companion of the 64-character rejection
key data of exactly 1024 base64url characters (the cap) forms a valid, listed Device - whois derives the Device Tag without importing the key; boundary companion of check's over-1024 taint case

identifier publishing include records lists them under includes, ordered by grant tag, refs in either spelling (identifier or identity domain) - the jane grant's tag equals the first segment of check's delegated composite deviceTag
a foreign-domain include ref is listed under the default (any) include policy
SECURITY: a foreign-domain include ref is not listed under an include=local policy
a foreign-domain include ref is listed when the endpoint record's include option allowlists its domain
an identity publishing only include records resolves with status 1, an empty devices list, and its grants under includes
SECURITY: endpoint triauth record with dnssec:false caps the resolution-level secure to false even though the include records are DNSSEC-validated
SECURITY: an include with an unrecognized critical option is not listed (fail closed); x- experimental options are retained
an include ref with a `+` in its username is not an Identifier, so the record is ignored
an include grant carrying a scope option is listed with scope in options and a grant tag that folds it - scope narrows where the grant works, and the tag pins its exact terms
SECURITY: an include whose scope carries one bad entry (scope=mail.google.com,|garbage|) is not listed - the whole record is ignored, never repaired to the valid entries
SECURITY: an include whose scope is the reserved word none is not listed - none is never a valid entry; any as the sole entry is the spelling that covers every service host
SECURITY: an include record publishing no scope option is not listed - scope is required, and an absent option is never defaulted
SECURITY: an include whose scope lists any beside a host (scope=any,mail.google.com) is not listed - any is only the sole-entry spelling, so the record is ignored as a whole
SECURITY: an include whose scope is ANY (uppercase) is not listed - scope values are literal and case-sensitive
an include grant scoped to an IPv4 literal and a single-label host (scope=10.0.0.5,localhost) is listed - scope entries cover every host a callback URL can carry
GROUPS: whois surfaces groups as fully-qualified names, qualified from the identifier's domain and sorted ascending
GROUPS: multiple groups records union; duplicate names dedupe silently
GROUPS: an uppercase record value is lowercased before grammar validation - names surface normalized
GROUPS SECURITY: a trailing comma (empty element) voids the whole groups record; sibling records stay effective
GROUPS SECURITY: one grammar-invalid element voids the whole record - never repaired to the valid subset
GROUPS SECURITY: an unknown critical option voids the groups record
GROUPS: an x- option is inert - the groups record still counts
GROUPS: names beyond the maxGroups cap are dropped in processing order - duplicates never consume the cap
GROUPS: a 20-byte name is kept; a 21-byte name voids its record (byte-size boundary of the device-name grammar)
GROUPS SECURITY: escapes are literal in a groups value - '%' fails the name grammar and voids the record (only profile values percent-decode)
GROUPS: kitchen-sink identity (keys + includes + profile + groups) - no cross-interference between record families
GROUPS SECURITY: a non-ASCII uppercase letter (U+212A KELVIN SIGN) is not ASCII-lowercased - the name fails the grammar and voids the record; siblings stay effective
SECURITY: an include ref with a non-ASCII uppercase letter (U+212A) is not ASCII-lowercased and the record is ignored - the ref grammar stays ASCII
GROUPS: names sort by bare name before qualification - a proper prefix (dev) precedes its extension (dev-ops)
SECURITY: an escaped option value is literal - use=a%75th is not 'auth', so the unknown flow taints the device (machine vocabularies never decode)
SECURITY: an include ref is literal - include jane%40triauthdemo.org contains '%', fails both ref shapes, and the grant is ignored
a profile value whose decoding fails (stray '%') is ignored - sibling records unaffected
a record value carrying a raw control character is ignored as a whole (not a Normal String) - escapes no longer manufacture one
an option value carrying a raw control character voids the whole record (not a Normal String); sibling records unaffected

PRIVATE: whois of an identifier under a private-mode domain called without a lookup code returns status:0 with identityDomain:null - no identity domain derives without the code, so the zone stays unenumerable and unconfirmable through this surface

PRIVATE: whois with the identity's lookup code resolves an identifier under a private-mode domain - status:1, identityDomain is the code-derived label, and devices list the bare device digest (the ~lookupCode suffix is what verification results and check carry); a same-domain include grant is listed like under any mode

PRIVATE: a triauth record without a mode option runs the domain in private mode by default - whois with the identity's lookup code resolves status:1 at the code-derived label, and the endpoint options report the defaults (mode=private, include=any)

PRIVATE: a well-formed lookup code the identity was not published under (bot's code for john) derives a label holding no records - status:0 with the derived identityDomain, so a wrong code is indistinguishable from a missing identity

PRIVATE SECURITY: the identity's lookup code, but records bound to another derivation (bot's commitment published at john's label) - the commitment gate fails the resolution, status:0 with identityDomain set and no records surfaced
PRIVATE SECURITY: records at the derived label with no commit record are not an identity - status:0 (the commit binding is required, never optional)
PRIVATE SECURITY: two commit records at the derived label (the label-merge tripwire) fail closed - status:0 even though one of them is the matching commitment

PRIVATE: a lookup code supplied under a public-mode domain is inert - status:1 identical to the code-less lookup (john._at.triauthdemo.org, bare deviceTag); nothing in the result names the unconsumed code

API: a lowercase lookup code (k7qj3fb9m2wzx0c4) fails the lookup-code grammar and is rejected with error 101 before any DNS lookup (the endpoint answer is a SERVFAIL that would surface as 110) - a caller-supplied code is never repaired, no case folding
API: a 15-character lookup code (K7QJ3FB9M2WZX0C) is rejected with error 101 before any DNS lookup - the grammar is exactly 16 characters of [A-Z0-9]
API: a misspelled option key (lookupcode) is rejected with error 102 before any DNS lookup - option keys are exact, so a typo never silently degrades into a code-less lookup

API: a config override object in the options position ({logger: null}) is rejected with error 102 before any DNS lookup - option keys are refused before the identifier is even consulted, and config overrides ride as the second argument: whois({identifier, lookupCode?}, config)
API: no arguments at all returns 102 - whois takes one options object, and an absent argument is refused before any other check
API: a null options argument returns 102 - whois takes one options object, and null is refused before any other check
API: an array in the options position returns 102 - whois takes one options object, never a positional argument list

API: a bare identifier string in the options position (john@triauthdemo.org) is rejected with error 102 before any DNS lookup - the identifier travels as options.identifier, and a string is never coerced into one
API: a lookup code without an identifier ({lookupCode}) is rejected with error 101 before any DNS lookup - a Lookup Code alone names no identity; options.identifier is required
